waypoints.name: Eldorado Creek Trailhead (Cascade River Road)
waypoints.directions: Drive Cascade River Road to its end at the Eldorado trailhead, about mile 20, at roughly 2,100 feet. The road usually doesn't open until late May or June, depending on snowpack. Camping in the Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier zone is a high-occupancy area requiring an advance wilderness permit reservation, so arrange that before you drive up.

waypoints.name: Eldorado / Inspiration Glacier camp
waypoints.directions: Walk about 90 ft back down the road and cross the Cascade River on the log, then go about 100 ft straight away from the river to the climbers' path. It climbs steeply through timber for about 1,500 ft to a boulder field; follow cairns up it, staying climber's right of Eldorado Creek, into Eldorado Creek Basin. Cross the ridge at about 6,100 ft into Roush Basin, take talus and slabs onto the Eldorado Glacier, rope up, and climb it to camp near 7,500 ft.

waypoints.name: Base of northwest couloir
waypoints.directions: Roped, cross the glacier past the East Ridge and head for the obvious notch between Eldorado's North Ridge and the first rock spire (Dean's Tower), at about 8,100 ft. Rappel from the piton anchor on the far side into the Marble Creek cirque (one 60 m rope does it), then traverse a few hundred feet across the small glacier to the foot of the couloir near 7,800 ft. A moat or bergschrund there widens through the summer.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Peak summit
waypoints.directions: Climb the couloir that splits the northwest face, about 1,000 ft of short ice steps separated by lower-angle snow, to a small flat area just below the summit ridge. From there follow the exposed snow knife-edge to the summit.
